name: Init Publish Rules for Both Hosts

pr.title: Have init allow both publish commands for Claude Code and Codex, inside a repository or not
pr.head: 4772318a26d706d5e3868c903ac96e5ff26945c3

summary: project init used to add one Claude Code allow rule, for project review publish, and failed outside a Git repository. Codex's approval reviewer then refused project summary publish twice as sending repository content to another host, so summaries stopped at local previews.

This change covers both publish commands on both hosts. The user's Claude Code settings gain Bash(project summary publish *) beside the review rule. Where Codex's configuration directory already exists, init writes a Projector-owned rules/projector.rules holding one prefix_rule that allows project review publish and project summary publish. Outside a repository, init now sets up only those two user-level files, says on stderr whether it wrote them or only reported them, and exits 0.
The terminal, --publish-rule, --no-publish-rule and review.publish_rule decide both hosts together. Without a terminal, init only reports each file as kept and says how to add the rules.

cards.title: What the reviews settled
cards.html:
• Fixed in 62c0dc2: outside a repository without a terminal, init said it set up rules it had only reported. The note now follows each file's action: all kept, some kept, or none.
  • Fixed in 9a25b74: docs/cli.md now says init manages two of your files and names the four reasons it keeps projector.rules.
  • Taken in 4772318: the README names both rules files, the docs and the Codex kept note show the rule, one read_user_file helper reads both files, and new tests cover the Codex writer's kept cases and its write through a link.
  • Checked: codex execpolicy check allows exactly the two publish commands under the written file, the documented rule, and the one-line rule.

groups.title: The rules and the two writers
groups.kicker: What init writes into each host's user settings, and how it handles a file it cannot use
intro: RULES replaces the single RULE with both Claude Code patterns. CODEX_RULES is the whole Codex file. Codex loads every *.rules file in its rules/ directory and saves the approvals a person grants to default.rules. So Projector owns projector.rules and rewrites it whole rather than merging into the user's file.

allow_publish now returns a list: the Claude Code action from allow_in_claude, plus a Codex action from allow_in_codex when codex_home() ($CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex) is a directory. Both writers read through read_user_file, which returns the text or the reason init cannot use the file. Both write through symlinks with write_through. A file they cannot use is kept with a note: the Claude Code note names the two rules, and the Codex note gives CODEX_RULE, the one-line rule to add.
concepts: A Codex prefix_rule with decision = "allow" runs the matched command without prompting and outside Codex's sandbox.
Codex counts as installed only when its configuration directory exists, so init never creates one.

checks.text: allow_in_claude appends only the missing rules, so a file holding only the review rule gains the summary rule and keeps the user's order.
The pattern ["project", ["review", "summary"], "publish"] matches the two publish commands and nothing else, such as project summary init or project site serve.
allow_in_codex reports unchanged only when the file is byte-for-byte CODEX_RULES, so a hand edit is overwritten and reported updated.
CODEX_RULE, the one-line rule in the kept note, matches the pattern and decision in CODEX_RULES, so following the note gives the same allowance.

files.note: The two rule constants, codex_home, and the new allow_in_codex beside the renamed allow_in_claude.

groups.title: One decision, and init outside a repository
groups.kicker: How the CLI decides the rules once for both hosts, and what init does where there is no repository
intro: publish_rule_mode lifts the inline decision out of run so both paths share it. It returns "add", "report", or None.

run now catches the EnvironmentError that discover_git_root raises, for init only, and hands off to init_permissions_only. That path refuses --site and --url with exit 2, writes only the user's rules files, and reports them. Its closing stderr note is worded from the files' actions: it says it added no rules when every file was kept, some when only some were, and that it set them up only when none was kept. emit_files gains readme=False, so that path's JSON lists only files, with no top-level action or path describing a projects README that does not exist.
concepts: In a repository, the top-level action and path in --json still describe the projects README, for older consumers.

checks.text: The closing note in init_permissions_only claims rules were set up only when no file is kept, so an agent relaying it never reports a rule the next publish still lacks.
Only init falls through to init_permissions_only; every other command still raises on a missing repository.
In a repository, publish_rule_mode still runs before any file is written, so a bad review.publish_rule refuses first.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Every test that reaches the writers runs under a temporary HOME
intro: RepositoryTestCase already pointed HOME at a temporary directory and unset CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. It now also unsets CODEX_HOME, so a real Codex configuration cannot be reached. New tests cover the summary rule joining an existing review rule; the Codex file created, unchanged, and restored; CODEX_HOME; no Codex directory; report mode; init outside a repository; and a codex execpolicy check of the rule, which is skipped where codex is missing. Later commits add tests for the all-kept and partly-kept notes outside a repository, for each way the Codex writer keeps projector.rules, and for its write through a link.

checks.text: Every new test runs under the suite's temporary HOME, and the link test's target is its own temporary directory, so no test reaches a real Claude Code or Codex configuration.

groups.title: Documentation and skills
groups.kicker: The CLI reference and the two skills that tell an agent what to do when a publish is refused
intro: docs/cli.md describes the second Claude Code rule, the Codex rules file with the rule it holds and when init keeps it, and init outside a repository. It also says that Codex runs an allowed command without asking and outside its sandbox. The README names both rules files. summarize-pr gains the instruction review-pr already had: when a host refuses publish, do not retry it in another form, and ask the user to run project init in a terminal or to run publish themselves. review-pr now mentions the Codex rules too.

checks.text: docs/cli.md says init manages two of your files, and its list of reasons for keeping projector.rules matches read_user_file and the write failure in allow_in_codex.
Both skills say init adds the rules only for a person at a terminal, so an agent never runs it to add them.

files.note: The new Codex entry, and the paragraph on init outside a repository.
